page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Spawn
steps.margin_note: One line for what it is and one for who releases it.
lines: Spawn is the mass of eggs released into the
It is seen in frogs and in other lower aquatic
steps.why: The two words name the two gametes released into water, so each is fixed by the sex that releases it.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two words. Spawn is eggs from the female; milt is sperms from the male.
Writing that spawn is laid on land. It is released into water.
steps.memory_tip: Spawn has the same s as she: eggs from the female. Milt has the m of male.

steps.label: Milt
steps.margin_note: Give the contrast in one boxed line, then add that fertilisation is external.

lines.text: Spawn: eggs, female · Milt: sperms, male

lines: Milt is the mass of sperms released into the
The male releases the milt over the spawn, so
steps.why: Naming where the two masses meet explains why frogs need no copulatory organ: the gametes are shed together in water.
common_mistakes: Calling milt a gland. It is the mass of sperms itself.
Writing that fertilisation is internal. The milt meets the spawn outside the body.
steps.memory_tip: Milt over spawn in the water: that is external fertilisation in one picture.

insider_note: The examiner accepts a one-line contrast, but the external fertilisation line is what lifts a half answer to a full one.
